title: Crucifixion of Christ
definition: The crucifixion of Christ is the historical death of Jesus on the cross, where He was condemned, nailed, lifted up, and killed for sinners.
summary: Jesus was crucified according to God's saving purpose and for the redemption of sinners.
christFocus: The crucified Christ reveals the seriousness of sin, the justice of God, and the depth of divine love.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The crucifixion was a real historical execution. Jesus was mocked, condemned, nailed to a cross, and died. Scripture does not present this as defeat but as the central act of redemption.

At the cross, human evil and divine purpose meet. Wicked hands crucified Him, yet God accomplished salvation through His death.

The crucifixion shows the cost of sin and the love of Christ for sinners.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People can become familiar with the cross and lose sight of its seriousness. The crucifixion matters because salvation came through the suffering and death of the Son of God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Look at the cross with reverence and gratitude. Confess sin honestly, trust Christ's finished work, and live as one bought at great cost.
